$comment: Ground truth. Never place this directory in scope for a tool being scored -- use `python pack.py` to produce a blind copy that provably contains only the cases.

01-receipt-export.summary: The query selects by id with no org_id predicate, so any authenticated caller exports any organization's receipts by guessing ids. The comment claims the UI only shows the caller's own org; the UI is not the boundary.
01-receipt-export.root_cause: authorization enforced in the presentation layer, absent from the query
01-receipt-export.fix: add `AND org_id = ?` bound to actor['org_id'] to the SELECT
01-receipt-export.decoy_shape: the f-string builds only `?` placeholders and the ids are parameterized, so the SQL-injection reading is wrong

02-report-sort.summary: The sort key is mapped through a dict of literals and anything else raises. No value derived from the request reaches the query text; org_id is parameterized.
02-report-sort.why_it_looks_bad: an f-string builds the ORDER BY clause, which is the canonical SQL-injection shape

03-avatar-import.summary: validate() resolves and checks the hostname, then urlopen follows redirects to a destination that was never checked. It is also a TOCTOU: the DNS answer used for the check is not the one used for the connection.
03-avatar-import.root_cause: the allowlist is applied to the requested URL rather than to every destination actually connected to
03-avatar-import.fix: disable redirect following (a urllib opener with a no-op HTTPRedirectHandler) and re-validate any destination before connecting; pin the resolved address for the connection

04-doc-thumbnail.summary: subprocess.run is given an argument list with no shell, the document id must parse as a UUID before it is used in a path, and page is range-checked. Neither path traversal nor command injection is reachable.
04-doc-thumbnail.why_it_looks_bad: subprocess plus request-derived arguments is the canonical command-injection shape

05-reset-token.summary: The token is sha256 of user id and the current unix second, both guessable. An attacker who knows a target's id computes candidates over a small time window and takes over the account. Tokens also never expire and are not single-use per issuance window.
05-reset-token.root_cause: a hash of low-entropy known values used where a random secret is required
05-reset-token.fix: secrets.token_urlsafe(32), stored hashed, with an expiry checked on consume

06-webhook-refund.boundary: exactly-once processing of a money event
06-webhook-refund.summary: The signature is verified correctly with compare_digest, but a validly signed body may be replayed indefinitely. Each replay credits the balance again. The provider itself documents at-least-once delivery, so this fires without an attacker.
06-webhook-refund.root_cause: no idempotency on the event id and no timestamp window; signature verification answers authenticity, not freshness or uniqueness
06-webhook-refund.fix: record the provider event id and reject an id already processed, inside the same transaction as the credit
06-webhook-refund.decoy_shape: the HMAC comparison is correct and is not the bug

07-credit-redeem.boundary: single-use invariant on a money object
07-credit-redeem.summary: Check-then-act across two statements with no atomicity. Concurrent requests all read redeemed_by as NULL and each credits the balance, so one code is redeemed many times.
07-credit-redeem.root_cause: the single-use invariant is enforced by a prior SELECT rather than by the UPDATE itself
07-credit-redeem.fix: UPDATE credit_code SET redeemed_by = ? WHERE id = ? AND redeemed_by IS NULL, then credit only if rowcount == 1, in one transaction

08-invite-accept.boundary: tenant data exposure on an unauthenticated route
08-invite-accept.summary: The #4412 fix was applied to accept_invite only. preview_invite still takes org_id from the query string and returns that organization's name, plan, seat count and billing email to an unauthenticated caller holding any valid invite token.
08-invite-accept.root_cause: a remediation applied at one call site rather than at the invariant; the sibling route kept the original pattern
08-invite-accept.fix: read the org from invite['org_id'] in preview_invite too, and return only the fields the landing page needs

09-archive-extract.summary: Zip Slip. Only absolute paths are rejected; a member named ../../etc/app/config.py writes outside the workspace. mkdir(parents=True) happily creates the traversed directories.
09-archive-extract.root_cause: the check tests the spelling of the path rather than where it resolves to
09-archive-extract.fix: resolve the destination and require it to be relative to the resolved workspace before opening it for write; refuse symlink members

10-cache-key.summary: MD5 names a derived image in the service's own cache. It is not a credential, not an integrity check, and never compared against attacker-supplied input; the inputs are a service-assigned UUID and two bounded integers.
10-cache-key.why_it_looks_bad: hashlib.md5 matches every weak-crypto rule ever written
